sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The major soldier differs markedly from M. natalensis: apart from the frontal sculpture and the shape of the mandibles, the outline and the colour of the head also differ. Head elongate, the sides nearly parallel and slightly straight, the posterior part slightly wider than the anterior; frontal area with a distinct depression, often continued as a narrow triangle across the fontanelle, so that the fontanelle lies in a shallow groove; fontanelle distinct and slightly raised, with a pair of small but clearly discernible raised dots at each side and in front. Antenna 17-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 4, most apical segments bead-like.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head and antennae reddish brown; body dirty brown; legs pale yellow, only the tarsi tinged with brown. Head elongate, the sides nearly parallel and slightly straight, the posterior part slightly wider than the anterior. Frontal area with a distinct depression, tending to continue as a narrow triangle across the fontanelle, so that in some specimens the fontanelle lies in a shallow groove; fontanelle fairly distinct and slightly raised, with a pair of small, clear raised dots at each side and in front; within the depression, about halfway from the anterior margin of the clypeus to the fontanelle, a low triangular swelling divided in two by a transverse wrinkle. Antenna 17-segmented; segment 3 longer than segment 4; most apical segments bead-like. Measurements: total length 14 mm; head length including mandibles 7.0 mm; head width 3.5—3.6 mm; left mandible length 2.1 mm. Minor soldier: smaller, the head paler yellow than in the major soldier, the mandibles proportionally longer, straighter and more slender. Frontal depression inconspicuous; fontanelle distinct; the paired raised dots at each side of and in front of the fontanelle as in the major soldier; no median swelling, the swelling only at the clypeus. Antenna 17-segmented, segment 3 about as long as segment 4 or slightly shorter. Measurements: head length including mandibles 3.9 mm; head width 1.9—2.0 mm; left mandible length 1.6 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Only one worker caste occurs in the series. Head yellowish brown; body dirty coloured; legs yellow; the base of the antenna distinctly pale, turning dark brown toward the apex.

note: Adapted from the original description by Fuller 1922 (in English), where the species was named Macrotermes ukuzii sp. n.; the description covers the major soldier, the minor soldier and the worker, while the alate is not described. The measurements in the original are all in millimetres (printed with hyphens as decimal points, such as "3-5" and "7-0"), and have been transcribed as 3.5 and 7.0; the total length of the minor soldier is damaged in the scanned text and is not listed.
